results.summary_before: This project is an experiment in using two-phase nonoverlapping clocks to make a design immune to hold violations, implemented by patching the flip-flops of Simon's Caterpillar into pairs of latches. It adds a scan chain through every flip-flop for debugging and disables static timing analysis by marking all paths as false paths. The design drives a seven-segment display, LEDs and a speaker, and requires a Simon Says PMOD plus two 50 kHz clocks with 25 percent duty cycle at 0 and 180 degrees. Silicon testing by the author reports it works as intended, with a bring-up script provided for the two-phase clock setup.

results.summary_before: This Verilog peripheral generates a bit clock for a PDM microphone and decodes the returned density signal into PCM words. It is configured through parameters for clock period and enable, and connects to the microphone via clock and data pins. Silicon testing with an MP34DT01-M breakout succeeded, capturing five seconds of audio while clocked from an RP2350 SPI interface. The design is notable for having a verified working silicon test report.
